subject: biotechnology
title: Fermentation: Yeast Converts Glucose to Ethanol and Carbon Dioxide

slides.heading: Fermentation: Yeast Converts Glucose to Ethanol and Carbon Dioxide
bullets: How yeast in one flask turns glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide over time: the glucose bar falls as the yeast consumes it, the ethanol bar rises, and carbon dioxide bubbles rise through the liquid and collect in the gas space
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we watch one flask, where nothing appears from nothing - the glucose is converted, step by step, into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain fermentation as a conversion: yeast takes in glucose and produces ethanol and carbon dioxide
Run the change in order: yeast added with the glucose bar full, glucose falls as ethanol and gas appear, glucose low with ethanol and gas grown, glucose used up with the products complete
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to say where every bit of ethanol and gas came from.

slides.heading: Ethanol and bubbles appear - so they came from nothing, right?
bullets: At the start the flask holds glucose solution and yeast - no ethanol and no collected gas
By the end there is ethanol in the liquid and a gas space full of carbon dioxide - where did they come from?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if the products were not there at the start, were they created from nothing? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation shows the glucose bar falling by exactly the amount converted.

slides.heading: Fermentation converts glucose - nothing appears from nothing
bullets: Yeast is a living organism: it takes in glucose and converts it, producing ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas
Every amount of ethanol and gas produced is paid for by glucose used up - the glucose bar falls by the amount converted
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: conversion, not creation - the material of the glucose reappears as ethanol and carbon dioxide.

slides.heading: Add yeast: living cells enter the glucose solution
bullets: Yeast is added to a flask of glucose solution: the glucose bar is full and there is no ethanol yet
Nothing has been converted at this stage: the flask holds glucose plus living yeast cells
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the full glucose bar and the empty gas space: this is the before picture.

slides.heading: Fermentation begins: glucose falls, ethanol and gas appear
bullets: The yeast takes in glucose, so the glucose bar begins to fall as consumption starts
Ethanol appears in the liquid and carbon dioxide bubbles form, rise through the liquid and reach the gas space
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow one bubble up: the products appear at the same time as the glucose falls - that timing is the conversion.

slides.heading: Conversion continues: glucose low, ethanol and gas grow
bullets: More glucose is converted: the glucose bar is low and the ethanol bar keeps rising
More carbon dioxide bubbles rise and collect in the gas space above the liquid
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and compare the three measures: glucose low, ethanol higher, gas space filling - one change, three views.

slides.heading: Complete: glucose used up, ethanol and carbon dioxide produced
bullets: The glucose is almost gone because it was converted: the ethanol bar is high
The gas space is full of collected carbon dioxide - the products came from the glucose, not from nothing
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and note the careful wording: glucose used up, not glucose vanished - it reappears as ethanol and carbon dioxide.

slides.heading: Worked example: tracking one flask from start to finish
bullets: Start: glucose full, no ethanol, gas space empty, yeast just added
Finish: glucose almost zero, ethanol high, gas space full - the glucose fell by the amount converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, yeast added, glucose full. Step 2, glucose falls as ethanol and gas appear. Step 3, glucose low, products grow. Step 4, glucose used up, products complete. At each step ask: what did the glucose become?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the conversion in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from yeast added to the glucose solution, state each stage in order and what happens to the glucose, the ethanol and the gas at that stage
Then swap and check: did your partner show the glucose falling as the products appear, or the products appearing from nothing?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full conversion in order, then take two pairs answers: glucose full, glucose falls, glucose low, glucose used up - with ethanol and carbon dioxide growing to match.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the alcohol appears from nothing while the glucose stays the same
Name what happens to the glucose as the ethanol and carbon dioxide are produced to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers track the glucose bar falling by the amount converted.
